claude-code+claude-opus-5@max.answer:
# Answer

**The leftmost red-robed performer would exit through the RIGHT-HAND side of the frame.**

## Who the subject is

The image shows a night-time masked-dance performance (Chhau-style, with huge spiked crown/halo headdresses) on a stage in front of a red-floodlit temple. At the far left of the frame there is a closely overlapping pair of dancers. The nearer-left one of that pair wears a **white/silver** costume with a cream dhoti, so it is not the subject. The subject is the figure immediately to its right — the first performer from the left dressed in **red robes**: a red draped over-garment studded with a column of round rosette medallions, red dhoti/trousers, and white cloth ankle wraps. It stands roughly one-eighth of the way in from the left edge of the picture, holding a thin stick (a bow/arrow) in the hand on its right side, angled down and to the right.

## Which way the subject is facing

The dancer is standing in near-profile, facing **screen-right** (toward the centre of the stage, where the other performers and the kneeling silver-crowned figure are). Four independent cues agree:

1. **The feet.** Zoomed in on the bare feet below the white ankle wraps, both feet have their toes pointing to the **right**, with one foot placed slightly ahead of the other along the same floor line. That is the signature of a profile stance. For comparison, the small dancer further right in the picture, whose mask I can clearly see facing the camera, has its feet splayed in opposite directions (left foot toes pointing left, right foot toes pointing right) — a frontal stance. The subject's feet do not do that.

2. **The headdress.** The subject's spiked crown/halo appears as a narrow, nearly edge-on crescent, unlike the wide symmetric fans of the dancers who face toward or away from the camera. An edge-on halo means the dancer's facing direction is roughly perpendicular to the camera axis, i.e. an almost pure left/right profile. Furthermore, the crescent leans so that its top is displaced to the **left** of its base; since these crowns tilt backwards over the head, the back of the head is on the left.

3. **The hair / back of the head.** A prominent mass of black hair sits below and to the **left** of the silver crown base, with a pale strap (the mask's tie) along its left edge. On the dancers in this photo, that black mass plus strap is what the *back* of the head looks like (clearly visible on the large dancer at the right of the frame); the dancer who faces the camera shows a painted mask face and no such black mass. So the subject's nape is on the left and its masked face on the right.

4. **The held prop and arm.** The visible hand and the stick it grips project from the **right** side of the body — the forward-reaching arm for a right-facing figure. The comparable dancer in the middle of the frame holds its bow out on the same side.

## The resulting path

Walking straight forward means walking to the **right**, essentially parallel to the front of the stage (the edge-on headdress shows the motion is nearly parallel to the image plane, not receding into the background). From its position near the left edge, the dancer would therefore travel rightwards across almost the entire width of this very wide frame — past the small red dancer, the central dancer, the kneeling silver figure and the two dancers at the right — and finally leave the picture through the **right edge**.

For completeness: it would not exit left (that is behind it), and it would not simply shrink away into the background out of the top of the frame, because its direction of travel is across the camera's view rather than away from the camera.

**Answer: the right side.**
